blocks.text: QMBCertify.jl builds a semidefinite program whose optimum is a provable lower bound on the ground-state energy (the dual of a variational method: it squeezes $E_0$ from below, never above). It hard-codes the Heisenberg model's symmetries (translation, dihedral, $xyz$ permutation, sign, conjugate) to block-diagonalize the SDP. Relaxation order $d=4$ is the accuracy dial — the paper's own 2D value. All strengthening constraints (RDM positivity, state optimality) are off, matching the paper's official 2D example. Mosek 11 is the commercial SDP solver (free academic license).

blocks.label: Partial match
blocks.why: the certification pipeline is fully validated (all bounds sit below their ED/QMC references, Mosek OPTIMAL, residuals ~1e-7) and the run EXACTLY reproduces the paper's OLD [31] column — L=4 to 6 digits with the official example settings, L=6 to 6 digits once the full-range basis is used (extra=7). The NEW Table 8 column is not reachable with any shipped setting (a full knob sweep: SU2, rdm=8, lso, pso, extra — closes only part of the gap): the public repo implements the 2024 PRX relaxation (its README cites only that paper), while the 2026 paper's new structured reductions that produce the new column are not yet released in the code. Root cause, not a numerical fluke.
